text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B has a clear thesis stating driverless cars would be a great development because they could stop accidents and improve transportation, then organizes body paragraphs around each claim.", "quality": "Clear thesis and organized structure", "description": "The essay presents a focused position up front and develops it through distinct, logically ordered body paragraphs with a conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Essay B cites specific article details like speed sensors detecting skids and rollovers, Google's modified Toyota Prius using sensors to create a 3-D model, and Sergey Brin's vision.", "quality": "Specific evidence integration", "description": "The essay grounds each argument in concrete details from the source article rather than vague or general references."}, {"evidence": "Essay B explains how the evidence supports its claims, e.g., 'If a person does not have the reflexes to be able to stop their car on time, the car could help a great deal, and could save lives.'", "quality": "Reasoned elaboration", "description": "The essay connects evidence to consequences and explains why the cited facts matter for the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay A's argument is underdeveloped and largely repeats one idea about texting and driving, with little support from the article beyond a brief mention of fuel and flexibility.", "quality": "Argumentative depth", "description": "Essay B develops multiple substantive reasons with support, whereas Essay A offers only a thin, repetitive case."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses a formal academic register with proper paragraphing and transitions like 'First' and 'Lastly,' while Essay A contains informal phrasing and run-on sentences.", "quality": "Conventions and control", "description": "Essay B demonstrates stronger command of sentence structure, spelling, and paragraph organization appropriate to argumentative writing."}]}
